title: Approval Authority Matrix — Patient Hardship Discount Program
content:
For each level of the Patient Hardship Discount Program, the matrix below sets who approves, the time allowed for the determination, the reviews that must take place before approval, and how long an approved determination runs.

## Matrix

| Level | Approved by | Determination made within (calendar days after a complete application) | Financial counselor interview before approval | Medicaid screening before approval | Days to apply for Medicaid after a screening shows likely eligibility | Eligibility period, months from the effective date |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hardship Discount Level 1 (25%) | Billing office | 10 | Not required | Not required | 0 (no screening required) | 6 |
| Hardship Discount Level 2 (50%) | Billing office | 10 | Not required | Not required | 0 (no screening required) | 6 |
| Hardship Discount Level 3 (75%) | Billing office | 10 | Not required | Not required | 0 (no screening required) | 6 |
| Hardship Discount Level 4 (100%) | Billing office | 10 | Not required | Required | 30 calendar days | 6 |
| Catastrophic Medical Hardship | Business Office Director | 15 | Required | Not required | 0 (no screening required) | 12 |
| Presumptive Eligibility Discount | Billing office | 5 | Not required | Not required | 0 (no screening required) | 6 |

## Reading the matrix

- **Approved by** names who approves at the level: the billing office, or the Business Office Director.
- **Determination made within** counts calendar days after a complete application.
- **Interview** states whether a financial counselor interview is required before approval.
- **Medicaid screening** states whether the applicant must be screened for Medicaid eligibility before approval. Where screening is required, the next column gives the calendar days, after a screening shows likely Medicaid eligibility, within which the applicant must apply for Medicaid; 0 appears where no screening is required.
- **Eligibility period** is the number of months, from the effective date, for which the determination applies.

## Points of comparison

- Catastrophic Medical Hardship is the only level approved by the Business Office Director, the only level requiring an interview, and the level with the longest determination time (15 days) and longest eligibility period (12 months).
- Hardship Discount Level 4 (100%) is the only level requiring a Medicaid screening, with 30 calendar days to apply for Medicaid after a screening shows likely eligibility.
- The Presumptive Eligibility Discount has the shortest determination time, 5 calendar days.
